question: In Python, an if-statement is used to execute a block of code if a specified condition is true.
In Python, every if-statement must always be paired with an else-statement.
The syntax for an if-statement in Python requires the condition to be followed by a colon (:).
In Python, the elif keyword is used to specify a new condition to test, if the previous condition was true.
In Python, indentation is mandatory to define the block of code under an if-statement.
In Python, the not operator can be used to reverse the logic of the condition in an if-statement.
The expression inside an if-statement in Python can include logical operators like and, or, and not.
You can have multiple elif statements following a single if statement but only one else statement.
In Python, if-statements are capable of evaluating any object, not just boolean conditions.
Python's conditional expressions, often termed as one-liner if-statements, use the syntax: condition if expression else alternative.
